idiom_name: SitePrism::Page DSL (set_url, element, sections) over Capybara
implementation_notes: SitePrism is the dedicated Page Object Model DSL for Capybara: a page class subclasses SitePrism::Page, declares its URL with set_url/set_url_matcher, its elements with element :name, 'css' (collections with elements), and reusable fragments with section :menu, Menu, '#gbx3'; the test instantiates the class, calls load, and Capybara drives the real browser. What replaces the classic structure is the DSL's generated accessors plus Capybara's implicit waiting, so the page object is declarative rather than a hand-written wrapper; plain Capybara classes work too, but SitePrism is the established Ruby idiom. Keep methods private where possible and let tests assert.
code_sketch:
class Home < SitePrism::Page
  set_url '/index.htm'
  element :search_field, 'input[name="q"]'
  section :menu, Menu, '#gbx3'

  def search(term)
    search_field.send_keys(term)
    search_field.send_keys(:enter)
  end
end
# test: home = Home.new; home.load; home.search('Sausages')
pitfalls: SitePrism and Capybara sessions are per-thread: a page object created in one thread cannot be used in another, and parallel specs need Capybara.using_session or separate sessions.
Generated element accessors re-query through Capybara, but a value read into a local variable - or an element object kept across a navigation - is stale.
set_url_matcher and load verify the page eagerly; an over-strict matcher turns a harmless redirect into a suite-wide failure.
